pr.title: Read a review's fetched head from its own ref, not FETCH_HEAD
pr.head: c8a1870d1ab40aa7fe7e538dc79472c018ded65b

summary: When a review starts, project review setup fetches the pull request's head into the operator's checkout, the repository clone the review runs beside. It then confirms that the commit it fetched is the head SHA that GitHub reports, and refuses with the head moved when the two differ. project review move does the same when a review follows the head to a new commit.

Both commands read the fetched commit from FETCH_HEAD. Git rewrites that one file on every fetch in the checkout, so a fetch by another review, or by a summary publish, could land between the fetch and the read. setup then compared the wrong commit and refused, naming a SHA that was not on the pull request. A review loop running several reviews in one checkout hit this three times in one day.

This pull request makes each fetch write its commit to a ref that only this call uses, refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>. The call reads the commit from that ref and deletes the ref. The fetch also passes --no-write-fetch-head, so a review leaves the operator's own FETCH_HEAD as their last fetch wrote it. The check that the head moved keeps its meaning: it still compares the tip of the head branch, or of pull/<n>/head for a fork, with GitHub's SHA.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Operator checkout: the clone of the repository that a review runs beside. Several reviews can share it.
  • FETCH_HEAD: a file in .git/ where Git records what the latest fetch brought in. Every fetch rewrites it.
  • Temporary ref: refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>, written by one fetch and deleted right after the read.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review, of 5a9221c, found the head clean. It ran a concurrency reproduction: at the base, 52 of 80 parallel fetches read the wrong commit or a half-written FETCH_HEAD, and with the fix all 80 read the right commit. It suggested that the fetch stop writing FETCH_HEAD, which nothing read any more.

c8a1870 adds --no-write-fetch-head and a test for it. An incremental review found it clean, with no finding threads.

groups.title: Each fetch reads its own ref
groups.kicker: The fix in the review fetch, its test, and the docs that describe it
intro: fetch in review.py is the one function that brings a commit into the operator checkout for a review. fetch_head calls it twice, once for the head and once for the base, and both setup and move call fetch_head.

The function now passes Git a refspec, +<ref>:refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>, so the fetched commit lands in a ref named for this process and eight random hex digits. It reads that ref with rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}, and a finally block deletes the ref whether the read succeeds or fails. No other process writes that ref, so a concurrent fetch cannot change what the read returns. The fetch also passes --no-write-fetch-head, so it leaves FETCH_HEAD to the operator, who may have just fetched something to check out.

Two new tests cover the change. One simulates the race by rewriting FETCH_HEAD to another commit right after every fetch, and checks that setup still succeeds and leaves no ref under refs/projector/. The other writes a FETCH_HEAD before setup and checks that setup leaves it unchanged.

checks.text: Concurrent fetches read the right commit. In a scratch clone, 8 worker processes ran fetch 80 times for two branches while another process kept fetching a third. At this head all 80 returned the right commit. With the base's fetch, 25 returned the other branch's commit and 27 failed on a half-written FETCH_HEAD. Neither run left a ref behind. The same run at c8a1870 also returned the right commit all 80 times.
The full test suite passes at c8a1870: 1081 tests with 1 skipped, under Python 3.12. project check and both claude plugin validate runs pass.

files.note: fetch writes the fetched commit to a temporary ref, reads it, and deletes the ref, without writing FETCH_HEAD.

checks.text: The name joins the process ID with 32 random bits. The process ID is unique among live processes on one machine, and the random suffix separates two processes that share an ID across machines or PID namespaces. Nothing else in the repository reads or pushes refs/projector/review-fetch/.

In a scratch clone, a review fetch created no FETCH_HEAD where none existed, and left an existing one byte for byte. --no-write-fetch-head needs Git 2.29 or later. fetch_summaries in site/serve.py already passes it on every call.

The ref is deleted on every path that reaches the read. A KeyboardInterrupt raised during rev-parse still runs the deletion, and a fetch of a missing branch raises ReviewError without writing a ref. Both were run in a scratch clone.

files.note: Two setup tests: one rewrites FETCH_HEAD after every fetch, as a concurrent fetch would, and one checks that setup leaves the operator's FETCH_HEAD alone.

checks.text: Run against the base's review.py, this test fails with the head moved to 7fcf168 while it was fetched. It passes at this head.
Run against fetch as it was at 5a9221c, which still wrote FETCH_HEAD, this test fails. It passes at this head.

files.note: The setup reference says where the command reads each fetched commit, and that it neither reads nor writes FETCH_HEAD.
